findings.summary:
Feature review 1/5 of PLAYABLE-JOURNEY-LOCAL-01 at 66bc735 (pre-correction): CHANGES REQUESTED. The core protected design largely conforms to engineering v1.2 / ADR-E03-E05. adult-access.requireSessionInTransaction takes the issuer lock first and only inside owned transactions. play-service.authorize runs the private parent/founder guard before household → consent → request → revision → assignment, and runs it in the primary transaction, the confirm/ACK transaction and the acknowledged receipt. Migration 017 binds the initial Start atomically with deferred integrity. The founder history is a separate read-only path: it takes the founder issuer by snapshot, never touches the adult token or rows, and has no ACK/repair. The five exact /adult/journey routes and the strict /founder/journey prefix with requireFounder before and after are in place (my setup-4 minors are closed). Failing build2 tests 4-17 show real Start, lost reply, pending recovery, journal-boundary races and frozen content passing. The candidate is not tryable, for these reasons: (1) composition.close() always throws because the key callbacks deny while journals are still verifying, so the empty→journey→restart/same-play/timeline integration test never got past its first close; (2) the CLI Vite setup drops the project's alias/React/Tailwind config and /@vite/env, so every family page is blank; (3) the frozen landing's cross-port founder links fall into the strict Sec-Fetch-Site guard; (4) getDemoState hard-codes WORKING with missing=[]; (5) three of the six focused failures are test or harness defects that must be fixed honestly. What I read this round:
- In full: journey-composition, journey-local, journey-play, private-play-authority, journey-founder, journey-page, journey-onboarding, journey-client, adult-http, migration 017, REPORT, PLAYABLE_JOURNEY.md, both composition/UI test files, vite.config.ts, index.html, main.tsx, and all four logs.
- Targeted ranges: play-service 100-407, LoopFamilyHome 50-187, loop-auth 20-39 plus the journey grep, family-space 40-59, adult-access 50-74/205-229, cost-journal close, journey-play test 140-179.
Not read in full this round: the rest of play-service/LoopFamilyHome/family-space/adult-access/loop-auth, loop-journey-play.test.mjs lines 1-139 and 180-EOF, and the adopted worker files (retained from my setup reads as exact pinned blobs; journey-demo was only grepped). I ran nothing and verified no hashes. Final three runs, build, 04-C, six probes, seven native cases and the final feature PASS are all still required. Full cards stay OPEN, 07-A/B stay DONE, the quarantine stays UNKNOWN, synthetic data only.

findings.title: composition.close denies its own key callbacks while journals verify on close
findings.problem: close() sets closing=true first (line 80). keyForHousehold and keyForOperator (lines 114-115) then fail whenever closing is true. Service close (line 82) and journal close (line 84) still need those keys: cost-journal close runs verify() before delegate.close (cost-journal.mjs:183-189), which asks for household keys. That throws 'Local synthetic cost journal unavailable', and composition reports 'Local synthetic cleanup incomplete' (close diagnostic log; focused tests at lines 74, 110 and the UI harness). Every fresh close fails, the CLI exits 1, and the first integration test fails at its first empty-store close (test line 75). So none of the following has ever run end to end: prepareJourney, intro, Start/Test, reopen, same-play/trial/Start, timeline equality and withdrawal (lines 76-94). Reopen after real use, including the exact owner.journal_files directory match at line 110, is also unproven.
findings.fix_check: Keys remain derivable for the core's own service and journal close/verify, and are refused only after every journal and the DB have closed (for example with a separate 'accepting' flag that HTTP and getDemoState check). Closing has to stay fail-closed for new work. A fresh close succeeds, the full test at line 74 passes through restart, the same play, the same trial and Start, and an identical timeline, and the partial-key test passes. No journal verification is weakened.

findings.title: CLI Vite drops project alias/React/Tailwind config and /@vite/env; pages blank
findings.problem: createServer({configFile:false,...}) omits vite.config.ts, which supplies plugins:[react()], resolve.alias '@'→app root and Tailwind PostCSS. app/main.tsx statically imports page.tsx, and page.tsx imports '@/components' and '@/lib', so the module graph fails to resolve. The actual CLI showed a blank /loop-preview/join with 'Failed to resolve @/components/ui/progress'. In addition, the dev /@vite/client imports /@vite/env, which neither the CLI 'virtual' allowlist (line 22) nor adult-http assetPath (adult-http.mjs:10) admits. The landing's 'Start as the parent' therefore fails, and no family, setup or player page can render in the deliverable.
findings.fix_check: The CLI reuses the existing vite.config.ts through configFile or an equivalent import, with no package or config file changes, and overrides inline: middlewareMode, hmr:false, ws:false, fs.strict, and fs.allow limited to the app root. /@vite/env (and only the exact required virtual IDs) are admitted in both allowlists. A fresh CLI renders /loop-preview/join, setup and family with no import-analysis errors. Native evidence still shows exactly two 127.0.0.1 listeners and nothing on 24678.

findings.title: Frozen landing's cross-port founder links hit strict Sec-Fetch-Site guard
findings.problem: The adopted launcher landing on the parent origin links to founderOrigin/founder/queue, /founder/generation and /founder/review (journey-demo.mjs line 53). Both servers are on 127.0.0.1 with different ports, so a clicked link is a same-site, not same-origin, navigation. The strict guard rejects any Sec-Fetch-Site other than same-origin or none with 403 for every strict prefix, including page GETs. A tester following the frozen landing therefore gets a JSON 403 instead of the workbench. Root may not patch the worker landing.
findings.fix_check: Choose one and document it. Option 1: loop-auth admits only top-level document navigation GETs (Sec-Fetch-Mode navigate, Sec-Fetch-Dest document, no body) from same-site for the exact HTML page paths, while all APIs, .js/.css and POSTs keep same-origin plus the Origin, Host, cookie and requireFounder checks before and after. Option 2: the Root docs and the email give honest address-bar or founder-home instructions, and the landing link limitation is carried as a worker finding needing a re-reviewed pin. Native evidence covers the clicked cross-port links, and HTTP tests prove the API guards are unchanged.

findings.title: getDemoState hard-codes WORKING stages and missing:[] regardless of evidence
findings.problem: The landing and status lists are constants: capture, submit, readiness, play, save, reload, resume and activity are always WORKING, and nothing is MISSING. Today the parent pages are blank, close fails and no native proof exists, yet the landing would still tell a tester everything works. The spec requires the landing status to accurately distinguish working, simulated and missing, and the lists to describe verified capabilities. A static claim baked into runtime is unverified prose.
findings.fix_check: Each stage is either derived from actual startup capability checks, with unverified or unproven stages listed as MISSING, or explicitly labelled as wiring-only and kept MISSING until the source-bound final evidence exists. A test asserts that the lists partition all 13 stage IDs and that a failed asset or core capability moves the stage out of WORKING. Docs and email use the same wording.

findings.title: Three failing tests are harness defects; fix tests, not guards
findings.problem: (a) The missing-session check sends Cookie:'' because httpCall always merges the parent cookie. adult-http cookies() correctly rejects an empty header with 400, so the test does not model the no-header case (the independent probe still needs the true no-header 403). (b) loop-journey-ui.test.mjs line 48 clicks 'Test trial: check availability' right after the heading. That control renders only after the asynchronous context check sets available (LoopFamilyHome.tsx lines 102 and 120), so the test races. (c) In the founder history race at loop-journey-play.test.mjs:158, both operations queue on the same raw service's serial operation and on single-connection PGlite. The diagnostic shows completion at 5952 ms against a 5000 ms bound, so this is serialization latency, not a deadlock. None of these should be greened by loosening the parser, the Origin checks or the auth.
findings.fix_check: (a) A request with no Cookie header returns 403 and an empty or malformed Cookie returns 400, with both asserted. (b) The UI test waits for the enabled control, and also asserts the control is absent before context resolves. (c) The bound is justified by the recorded measurement or the test asserts completion order and outcome, keeping the no-40P01, no-row-change and both-complete assertions. The original failing logs are preserved, and all 19 focused tests pass on the corrected source.

findings.title: Founder ready retry with known command but pending binding fails as conflict
findings.problem: When bridge.status shows the command exists but the binding row is not yet committed or visible (uncertain readiness), ready() fails 'conflict' rather than reconciling the original key. The page's 'Make ready' retry then reports an error even though the spec says uncertainty uses original-key status/reconcile. The separate reconcile button works, but the primary retry path is misleading.
findings.fix_check: If the original command exists, ready() delegates to reconcile with the same command_id. It reports conflict only when an existing binding differs in snapshot, scope or command, and a test covers this.

findings.title: Help events never reconciled through saved journey/timeline path
findings.problem: The only help evidence is a standalone engine-2 dispatch unit test. The journey uses engine 1, so the timeline truthfully says 'unavailable_for_this_toy_pattern'. However, setup2 asked build2 integration to reconcile a scripted predict/config/Test/help sequence exactly against saved server events and the timeline. No test passes an accepted help action through raw play-service, journal and verifiedFounderHistory and shows help='recorded' with exact events.
findings.fix_check: A play-service or private-authority test with an engine-2 (assisted) private revision commits a help action and asserts that verifiedFounderHistory events equal the persisted play_events and that help is 'recorded'. Otherwise REPORT explicitly carries this as an unmet 09-A criterion.

findings.title: Post-reconsent profile save reports failure after committed setup
findings.problem: save() commits setup.save and then runs ensure() in a new transaction. activation_id is household-only, while the kernel digest is epoch-bound. After reconsent, an ordinary child profile correction commits but then throws a conflict from activateTrial, so the parent sees a failure for a saved change. A retry repeats the same error.
findings.fix_check: The post-save hook distinguishes 'trial already owned under an earlier epoch' (no mint; return the saved child plus an explicit trial state) from a genuine failure, with a test for reconsent followed by a correction. Alternatively, REPORT carries this as a known setup_unavailable limitation with UI copy.

findings.title: Journey Start pending is never shown; 503 throws before pending branch
findings.problem: journey_pending and retryable responses return HTTP 503. journey-client post() throws on any !ok, so LoopFamilyHome's 'Start pending… no second play' branch (line 112) is unreachable and the user sees 'Start not confirmed'. Retry still reuses the same command, so this is safe, but the pending state is not shown as specified. Action pending is handled correctly by the saved-player's 503 rule.
findings.fix_check: Either Start returns the validated pending body (for example as 202, like the other routes, with the client accepting it), or the UI copy and tests intentionally treat 503 as pending for Start too.

findings.title: Reading and evidence limits of this review
findings.problem: I did not read the following in full: play-service lines 1-99, LoopFamilyHome lines 1-49, family-space lines 1-39, the rest of adult-access, loop-auth lines 40-72 beyond the journey grep, tests/loop-journey-play.test.mjs lines 1-139 and 180-EOF, and docs JOURNEY_DEMO and SAVED_BINDING. I did not re-read the adopted worker files (pinned blobs retained from my setup reads; journey-demo only grepped). I ran nothing, verified no blob or SHA, and saw no independent probe run. Still missing: three consecutive full suites, build, 04-C, the six probes, seven source-bound native cases, a listener check and a final Claude feature PASS. The typecheck has 28 errors against a baseline of 27, with the new one in a worker file and carried.
findings.fix_check: The next feature review reads every changed Root file and test through EOF against the corrected commit. It also receives the immutable logs of the three-run sequence, the probes and the native cases, plus the recovery and correction-3 attempt records, and accounts for the remaining worker findings.
